provenance.not: not a new panel, not a pre-registration, not independent confirmation: the same 18 cells were examined in lunar panel v2 before this probe existed
provenance.statistic: adjusted R2 of the descriptor on the three declared axes, per 8-unit cell

invariance.family: z = g*(x*cos(theta) + y*sin(theta)); g=0.30, n=18, dx=500
invariance.claim: the three declared axes are exactly invariant under a quarter-turn rotation and under reflection about the diagonal, and NOT under a 45-degree rotation (relief moves through the bounded rho factor)

bank_quarter_turn.what: of the common bank scalars, those that are NOT invariant under theta -> theta+90 on a plane, relative tolerance 1e-9
bank_quarter_turn.why_it_matters: a descriptor invariant under the quarter turn cannot be shown non-redundant by this symmetry argument, so this list bounds what the analytic half can predict

nan_audit.what: cells where the ENGINE-STYLE fractional distance to the reference is undefined -- the reference value is 0 and the candidate value is not, or an input is non-finite
nan_audit.note: all three declared axes are strictly positive so the published panel is unaffected; the refusal is what stops a fraction added as an axis from silently deleting candidates, because the Pareto rule excludes any unit carrying a non-finite distance

circular_excluded.reason: circular quantity in degrees; a Euclidean Pareto distance on it is meaningless (359 deg and 1 deg are adjacent) and it is therefore reportable as a finding but not admissible as an axis

random_control.construction: uniformly random 4th coordinate per unit, same range normalisation

verdict.reading: The analytic half establishes that the three declared axes are exactly blind to a quarter-turn rotation of a planar surface, so a descriptor not invariant under it must carry information they do not -- and one does: the variogram nugget has a median adjusted R2 below zero, i.e. the three axes predict it no better than three random numbers would. The consequence half then shows that this axis changes the decision at ZERO of the 18 cells, while a uniformly random 4th coordinate changes it at about 15. The frontier is therefore not fragile to a BAD axis or robust to a GOOD one -- it is fragile to the NUMBER of axes, which is a property of running a Pareto rule over 8 units in 3 dimensions and not a property of any candidate. The published lunar sole-winner property must not be read as evidence about candidates; what the panel supports is the ranking it states, provisional, and nothing stronger.
verdict.what_this_does_not_show: It does not show that the declared axes are the wrong axes, nor that any Earth candidate is a better analog. Adding dimensions promotes co-winners without discriminating between them, so this experiment bounds a CLAIM, not a candidate.

controls.expected: an exact identity must be fully explained (1.000000); a different estimator of the same idea should be very high but not exact
